name: get_current_weather
description: Get the current weather for a place.

location.description: The city and optionally the country, e.g. "London" or "Paris, France". Leave it empty for where the user is (guessed from their IP address).

name: list_directory
description: List the files and directories in a directory of the user's home directory (directories end with /), or show it as a tree with depth. Dotfiles are left out unless hidden is true; places with keys, tokens, browser data or shell history are never shown. The user does not see what this returns: write the names out for them, as a list or the tree, when they want to see them.

path.description: The directory, e.g. "~" or "~/Documents"; relative paths are relative to the home directory.

depth.description: How many levels to show: 1 (the default) lists just this directory; 2 to 4 draw a tree of the directories in it, e.g. when the user asks for a tree.

hidden.description: Also show dotfiles and dot-directories (like .config or .zshrc), e.g. when the user asks about their config files.

name: read_file
description: Read a text file in the user's home directory (at most the first 64 KB), dotfiles and configs too, e.g. "~/.zshrc" or "~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua". Files with keys, tokens, browser data or shell history cannot be read.

path.description: The file, e.g. "~/Documents/notes.txt"; relative paths are relative to the home directory.

name: look_at_image
description: Look at a picture (PNG, JPEG or WebP) in the user's home directory and get a description of it. Call it when the user asks what is in an image, e.g. one of their wallpapers; you cannot see images otherwise.

path.description: The image file, e.g. "~/wallpapers/autumn.jpg"; relative paths are relative to the home directory. Use list_directory first if you do not know its name.

question.description: Optional: what the user wants to know about it, e.g. "is there a cat?".

name: list_todos
description: Show the user's todo list, numbered. Call it when the user asks what is on it, or before removing an item you are not sure of.

name: add_todo
description: Add an item to the user's todo list. Call it whenever the user asks you to remember, note, put on the list or add something to do; it is only added if you call this.

item.description: The item, short, in the user's words, e.g. "buy milk".

name: remove_todo
description: Remove one or more items from the user's todo list, when they are done or the user asks you to; they are only removed if you call this. To remove several, name them all in ONE call: the numbers change after a removal.

item.description: The item's number from list_todos, or (part of) its text; several separated by commas, e.g. "1, 4".

name: edit_todo
description: Change what an item on the user's todo list says, when the user wants it reworded or corrected (e.g. "change 1 to plant flowers"); it keeps its place. It is only changed if you call this.

item.description: The item's number from list_todos, or (part of) its current text.

text.description: What the item should say instead, short, in the user's words.

name: set_reminder
description: Set a reminder or a timer: the mascot tells the user when the time comes (or when Mascot next starts, if it is not running then). Call it whenever the user asks to be reminded of something or wants a timer; it is only set if you call this.

when.description: When, in the user's local time: a duration from now ("10m", "1h30m", "2 hours"), a time of day ("12:00", today or else tomorrow), "tomorrow 9:00", or a date and time ("2026-10-19 12:00").

text.description: What to remind of, short, in the user's words and language, e.g. "water the flowers"; for a plain timer say so, e.g. "timer, 10 min" (in their language).

name: list_reminders
description: Show the reminders and timers that are set, numbered, in time order.

name: cancel_reminder
description: Cancel a reminder or timer when the user asks you to; it is only cancelled if you call this.

item.description: The reminder's number from list_reminders, or (part of) its text.
